{{short description|Japanese Mathematical Biologist (born 1952)}}
{{BLP sources|date=March 2011}}
'''Yoh Iwasa''' (born 1952) is a Japanese Mathematical Biologist who is considered the leading mathematical biologist in Japan.<ref>''Supercooperators'' by [[Martin Nowak]] p 65</ref>

His work includes the evolution of costly mate preferences and the evolutionary dynamics of cancer.  Notable papers include:

* "The evolution of costly mate preferences II. The 'handicap' principle" ''Evolution'' 1991
* "Demographic theory for an open marine population with space-limited recruitment" with [[Joan Roughgarden]] ''Ecology'' 1985
* "Dynamics of chronic myeloid leukaemia" ''Nature'' 2005
* "Prey distribution as a factor determining the choice of optimal foraging strategy" ''The American Naturalist'' 1981 - JSTOR
* "Influence of nonlinear incidence rates upon the behavior of SIRS epidemiological models" with [[Simon Levin]] ''Journal of Mathematical Biology'', 1986

He has mentored more than 20 Ph.D. students and 20 Postdoctoral researchers. <ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bio-math10.biology.kyushu-u.ac.jp/english/member/ob_og.html|title=FORMER MEMBERS &#124; Mathematical Biology Laboratory Department of Biology, Kyushu University|access-date=2019-02-20|archive-date=2019-10-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191004150048/http://bio-math10.biology.kyushu-u.ac.jp/english/member/ob_og.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
